With Edge Commerce Stack, you can deploy a complete digital commerce stack in 48 hours, taking control of your online store and payment processing, even in the most isolated markets. This guide will explain how Google Apps Script can be used for digital commerce automation, a key component of our Edge Commerce Stack, and show you how to deploy it today.
What This Actually Is and Why It Matters

Digital commerce automation with Google Apps Script is a backend logic engine that enables you to automate tasks such as order processing, payment verification, and product delivery. This automation engine is built on top of Google Apps Script, a free service that allows you to run custom functions and build integrations with other services. By automating these tasks, you can reduce manual errors, improve customer satisfaction, and increase sales revenue.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The Edge Commerce Stack architecture uses Google Apps Script as the backend logic engine, which triggers a webhook to NOWPayments when a payment is confirmed. NOWPayments then fires another webhook to your Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, which updates your Supabase or Google Sheets order storage. Finally, your Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script sends a delivery email with the product link or download instructions to your customer using Resend or Gmail. This architecture ensures seamless automation of digital product delivery and payment processing.

Google Apps Script is the heartbeat of digital commerce automation, enabling automation of order processing, payment verification, and product delivery.
The Components That Make It Work Together

Cloudflare Workers is the backend engine in Stack 02 deployments. It runs serverless JavaScript at the edge — code that executes in response to HTTP requests, including the incoming NOWPayments webhook. The free tier provides 100,000 requests per day, which is sufficient for the sales volume of most individual digital product sellers. Workers has no server to manage, no runtime to configure, and no infrastructure to maintain. It scales automatically. It is globally distributed — the same code runs in data centers close to wherever the request originates, which means your webhook endpoint responds quickly regardless of where NOWPayments sends the request from. Cloudflare Workers integrates natively with Cloudflare R2 for file storage and Cloudflare D1 or external Supabase for database operations.

How does automated digital product delivery work with crypto payments?

Automated digital delivery works through a specific technical sequence that eliminates every manual step. NOWPayments monitors the blockchain for incoming transactions to your configured wallet address. When a transaction receives the configured number of on-chain confirmations — typically one confirmation on Tron, which takes under 60 seconds — NOWPayments sends an HTTP POST request to the webhook endpoint URL in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Your Cloudflare Worker or Google Apps Script Web App receives this request, validates the webhook signature against the secret key you configured, reads the payment amount and transaction hash from the payload, confirms the transaction independently on the blockchain, logs the order to your database, generates a receipt, creates a time-limited download link for the product file, and sends the delivery email. The entire sequence completes in under 30 seconds from payment confirmation in almost all cases. Nothing in this sequence requires your presence, your attention, or any manual action.
The Edge Commerce Stack uses a webhook pipeline to automate digital product delivery and payment processing, ensuring seamless order fulfillment and customer satisfaction.

Your Deployment Checklist

Deploy your backend first — Cloudflare Worker or Google Apps Script Web App — and confirm the endpoint URL is accessible via HTTP POST before configuring NOWPayments. Set the IPN webhook URL in your NOWPayments account settings to point to your backend endpoint. Set the IPN secret key in both NOWPayments and your backend configuration — this is the string that both sides use to verify webhook authenticity. Upload your product files to the configured delivery storage — Cloudflare R2 or Google Drive — with the paths matching your backend configuration. Complete a real mainnet transaction and check your backend logs to confirm the webhook was received, the signature was validated, the transaction was verified on-chain, the order was logged, and the delivery email was sent. Open your order database and confirm the order appears with correct status. Monitor the order database daily for the first week to confirm all orders are processing correctly. After a week of clean operation, move to checking for flagged exceptions every few days.
